tasks.short: Help clients resolve problems and use the service after signing.

steps.what: Discuss the problem, its impact and the client's desired outcome.
Find account history, service records and earlier support cases.
Check the agreement and service guidance for applicable remedies.

loop.input: Issue brief, relevant agreement sections and approved service guidance.
loop.output: Applicable obligations, possible remedies and unresolved questions, with source passages.
loop.check: Verify account access, document versions and citations; the seller checks applicability.
loop.stop: One retrieval pass and one revision; missing or conflicting terms go to the contract owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client descriptions and agreement wording vary; exact field matching misses relevant obligations.

steps.what: Discuss remedies and agree a proposed resolution with the client.
Approve remedies outside the seller's delegated limits.
Assign the agreed service fix and chase the responsible team.
Record the resolution, owner and next follow-up date.
Send the client a written resolution and progress update.

tasks.design: Join account history in the {CRM}, cases in the {HELPDESK} and agreement references in the {CLM} into one case view. A bounded reading step prepares a cited remedy brief; the seller handles the conversation and approval limits route exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}. Approved resolutions create service work orders, update the {CRM} and prepare client updates in the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account history, contract terms and delivery updates sit in separate places. Linking them and maintaining reliable handoffs often cost more than the perceived saving.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case routing and approval features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector effort, while a bounded reading loop handles varied issue descriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed obligations, delivery failures and damaged trust need context and negotiation. Source records can also disagree.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the client's real concern, repair trust and choose a proportionate remedy.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on recurring service failures across the seller's accounts.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time finding records and chasing updates, and more time resolving difficult cases. A weekly failure review becomes feasible; authority to grant remedies still follows delegated limits.

reach.task: Review recurring account problems and prioritise service improvements.
reach.learn: Separate isolated complaints from repeated failures and estimate account impact.

evidence.claim: Case joins, routing, reminders and structured record updates can use deterministic integration and workflow rules.
A cited reading assistant can prepare remedy options, but applicability and relationship repair remain human judgements.
The Air Canada case illustrates the consequences of incorrect automated service information; it does not establish outcomes for this occupation.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured results.
The baseline is an established service business with account records and a support process.
Exceptional approvals are averaged across cases; routine remedies use existing delegated limits.
A first version can use authorised exports and approved documents before write access is available.
GDPR applies to client data. National rules determine employee consultation requirements; access and applicable consultation are included in the estimate.
Build ranges cover one service line and working days; consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which system holds authoritative service status and account identifiers?
What remedies can the seller approve, and who approves exceptions?
Are agreements searchable and linked to the correct account?
Which access permissions and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Can account and case records be joined reliably without broadening access?
How often do approved remedies require interpretation beyond the available guidance?
new_work: Review cited remedy briefs and resolve conflicting documents.
Handle failed handoffs, overdue fixes and client updates requiring sensitive wording.
Maintain approval limits, document versions and account-to-case mappings.
Review recurring failure patterns with service delivery.

tasks.short: Answer questions about service options, prices, availability and agreed credit terms.

steps.what: Receive the question and clarify the service, account and requested date.

loop.input: Written customer question or seller-entered summary of a live question.
loop.output: Question category, service reference, account reference, requested date and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate references against permitted records; preserve the original question and flag ambiguity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved identity or meaning returns to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Written requests use varied language; structured forms cover only part of the intake.

steps.what: Find the relevant service description and approved answers.
Look up the current price and any agreed account discount.
Check service capacity and available delivery dates.
Check the account's approved payment and credit terms.
Explain the relevant options, price, availability and approved terms.

loop.input: Question brief and permission-filtered service, price, availability and credit facts.
loop.output: A concise answer with internal citations and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Prices, dates and terms must match source fields exactly; the seller approves before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing, stale or conflicting facts require a human answer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions; combined questions need short explanations adapted to the customer's wording.

steps.what: Discuss unusual requirements and refer requests for changed terms.

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} intake identifies the question, then retrieves approved service facts from the {DOCS}, prices from the {CRM}, capacity from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and existing credit terms from the {ERP}. Exact lookups and calculations run as rules; a bounded model drafts combined explanations with internal citations. The seller approves customer-facing answers, while changed prices, capacity commitments or credit terms follow existing approval routes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers require several lookups, and approved documents are often poorly indexed. Maintaining those joins and answer templates has required scarce implementation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, structured lookups and access controls handle the factual work. AI-assisted coding can make a small answer desk economical, with a model used only for intake and wording.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can change between lookup and commitment. Missing account terms and unusual requirements still need an authorised person.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what the customer is really asking and explain trade-offs without making unsupported promises.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time searching and more time on unusual requirements and buying concerns. No new pricing, capacity or credit decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Check account details and explain already approved payment terms.
reach.learn: Account identity checks, confidentiality boundaries and when finance approval is required.

evidence.claim: Approved-document answers with citations and deterministic price lookups are feasible building blocks.
The Air Canada case documents liability for incorrect chatbot information, supporting strict controls on customer-facing factual claims.
Article 50 requires disclosure for direct AI interaction unless it is obvious; it matters if a customer-facing AI channel is later introduced.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
Service guidance, price books and approved account terms have identifiable owners.
Availability is informational until a separate booking or service commitment is confirmed.
The solution reads existing credit terms; it does not score creditworthiness or decide new terms.
Live calls remain with the seller; no new call recording is assumed.
GDPR applies to account data. Access and any employee consultation required under national rules are included in the estimate.
An initial version can use authorised exports with visible freshness dates.
unknowns: Where do authoritative prices, account discounts and capacity records reside?
How current must each answer be before the seller can use it?
What proportion of questions arrive in writing versus live conversation?
Who approves exceptional prices, delivery promises and credit terms?
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which question categories can use exact approved answer blocks without a model?
Can the source systems expose freshness and account-level permissions reliably?
How much review time remains for combined questions during live calls?
new_work: Maintain service guidance, answer categories and price-source mappings.
Review generated wording before customer use.
Resolve missing terms, stale availability and conflicting source facts.
Sample answers for incorrect commitments and unnecessary disclosure of account data.

tasks.short: Prepare tailored sales presentations and proposals that explain the service.

steps.what: Confirm the client's objectives, requirements and buying concerns.
Collect account details and relevant opportunity notes.
Select service descriptions, specifications and approved examples.
Calculate the proposed service scope, quantities and indicative price.
Write and assemble the tailored proposal or presentation.

loop.input: Proposal brief, approved source pack, priced scope and fixed section structure.
loop.output: Tailored narrative inserted into a proposal or presentation template.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to approved sources; verify all prices and specifications against structured inputs.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported requirements remain visibly unresolved for the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill facts, but explaining how the service meets varied client objectives needs tailored prose.

steps.what: Check unusual specifications and delivery claims.
Approve the final proposal and send it to the client.

tasks.design: A proposal generator takes an approved brief from the {CRM}, selects tagged material from the {DOCS} and calculates scope and prices with deterministic rules. A bounded model writes the tailored explanation into fixed templates, with claims linked to their sources. Specialist checks and the seller's final approval precede sending through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful material is scattered across old proposals, and each seller repeats document assembly. A maintained template and pricing integration has often been too expensive for smaller service lines.
tasks.enabler_now: Template rendering, document tagging and pricing rules already work without models. AI-assisted coding lowers assembly costs, and a bounded drafting loop reduces rewriting.
tasks.still_hard: Poor discovery produces a polished but irrelevant proposal. Bespoke delivery promises and claims about outcomes still require expert judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the argument that matters to this buyer and recognise requirements the service cannot honestly meet.

ambition.what: Smaller accounts needing a tailored service proposal.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time assembling documents and can prepare tailored proposals for smaller opportunities. The seller gains room to choose which opportunities deserve tailoring; commercial approval limits still apply.

reach.task: Translate client requirements into a feasible service scope.
reach.learn: Service dependencies, exclusions and evidence needed to support delivery claims.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, deterministic pricing and bounded narrative drafting can be combined into a proposal generator.
Salesforce Agentforce for Revenue supports generating quotes from a typed request; this supports the quoting component, not the full proposed presentation workflow.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time in its own sales team, with no base or period given; this is not a forecast for this design.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
This baseline uses a maintained rate workbook where formal quoting is not fully configured in the {CRM}.
Existing quoting and template features should be configured first where they meet the need.
Approved material can be tagged by service and client need without a model.
Specialist review applies to unusual scope; its time share is averaged across proposals.
GDPR applies to client briefs. Confidential examples require permission for reuse.
Build estimates include access and applicable employee consultation under national rules; no seller scoring is introduced.
The first version covers one service family and can use authorised exports.
unknowns: Are prices governed in the {CRM}, a rate workbook or another authorised source?
Which examples and claims are approved for external reuse?
Which smaller opportunities currently receive only generic proposals?
What access and consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How much tailoring can approved conditional sections handle before a model is useful?
Can every factual claim in a sample proposal be traced to a current approved source?
Does the generated document remain readable across the required output formats?
new_work: Maintain templates, service tags, pricing rules and approved examples.
Review tailored narratives for relevance and unsupported claims.
Resolve gaps between requested and deliverable scope.
Check rendered documents after template changes.

tasks.short: Prepare sales forms and agreements from accepted commercial terms.

steps.what: Confirm the accepted offer, contracting entity and intended start date.
Collect customer, billing and signatory details.
Select the approved agreement template and required schedules.
Populate the agreement with the accepted scope, prices and terms.
Review and approve requested departures from standard clauses.
Approve the commercial agreement for issue.
Prepare the signature request and send the approved agreement.
Check signature status and remind outstanding signatories.
File the signed agreement and update the opportunity and service handover.

tasks.design: Populate approved templates in the {CLM} from accepted offer data in the {CRM} and billing details in the {ERP}, using fixed template and clause rules. The {WORKFLOW} routes departures and commercial approvals, then sends only the approved document version through the {ESIGN}. Signature events update the {CLM} and {CRM} and produce the service handover; no model is needed for the standard path.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer data, agreement templates and signature requests are disconnected. Template variation and unclear data ownership make seemingly simple copying difficult to automate reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing template, approval and signature features can handle the standard path. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of field mapping, validation and event handling without changing legal judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard liability, ambiguous scope and signatory authority remain difficult. A signed agreement must match the approved version exactly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a material departure from the deal and negotiate obligations the organisation can honour.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time copying fields, arranging signatures and filing agreements. No new authority to change clauses, accept risk or approve commercial terms is assumed.

reach.task: Validate the contract-to-service handover before service setup.
reach.learn: Mandatory order fields, billing dependencies and checks that prevent premature service activation.

evidence.claim: Teamleader provides customer records and quotes that can be signed online; its Focus AI acts after approval.
Template population, approval routing, signature reminders and signed-document filing can run deterministically.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
The accepted offer has structured scope, price and term fields; otherwise the seller must first confirm them.
Templates and clause rules are approved and versioned.
Legal review applies only to departures; standard agreements bypass that branch.
The signature step cannot alter the approved document or recipient list without renewed approval.
Reminder frequency is capped, and disputes or changed recipients return to the seller.
GDPR applies to contact and signatory data. National rules determine any employee consultation requirements, included alongside access in the estimate.
Build ranges cover one agreement family; authorised exports can support draft generation before write access is available.
unknowns: Which agreement templates and clause-selection rules are approved?
How complete and reliable are accepted-offer fields?
Who can approve commercial terms, legal departures and signatory details?
Which signature events and document certificates are available?
What access and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can the accepted offer populate every mandatory agreement field without interpretation?
Can the signature request be bound to the exact approved document version?
Can repeated signature events be processed without duplicate records or service handovers?
new_work: Maintain field mappings, templates and clause-selection rules.
Resolve missing details, signatory changes and nonstandard clauses.
Handle declined signatures, expired requests and failed synchronisation.
Check that approved, signed and archived document versions remain linked.

role.altitude: The week shifts from record searches, document assembly and chasing to discovery, difficult client conversations and service follow-through. Better preparation supports judgement, while pricing, credit and contractual authority remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Sales manager: turn repeated account problems into prioritised service improvements.
Sales engineer: translate client requirements into feasible, evidenced service scope.
Order clerk: validate complete, consistent service handovers.
New accounts clerk: check account details and explain approved payment terms.
skills_to_grow: Structured client discovery and concise requirements capture.
Service scoping, exclusions and evidence for commercial claims.
Reading approval limits and recognising contractual departures.
Checking source freshness, citations and account permissions.
Diagnosing workflow exceptions and maintaining reusable templates.
role.ambitious_version: A seller who can offer tailored proposals to smaller accounts and bring a weekly, evidence-based view of recurring service failures to the sales manager, while keeping sensitive commitments with authorised people.

job.title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
